source.document: RULINGS-NEEDED.md (lane spec132-move, branch wf2/spec-132, 2026-10-20): "Rulings needed: roles of Specs 120, 121 and 123"

decisions.question: Role of Spec 120: Pipeline Step Runner & Step Validator (1,211 lines). Today: Contradictory banner (NOT RATIFIED, plus "authorized registration"); Status UNRATIFIED DRAFT.
decisions.recommendation: **Recommendation.** Make Spec 120 **historical**. Replace the contradictory banner block with one historical banner, worded roughly: "Role: historical. The design record for the step runner; built and superseded by Spec 122 (standard) and Spec 124 (policy). Registered 2026-08-22 on 'the specs are good ratify'; never ratified as a standard." Keep the false-ratification incident as a dated note under the banner, not as the header. The Status line becomes `HISTORICAL`. Code citations to `Spec 120 §x` stay valid as history. The historical-spec rule then stops any new rule id from landing in Spec 120.
decisions.summary_recommendation: historical; one banner; dated incident note

decisions.question: Role of Spec 121: Assessment & Verification Methodology (2,689 lines). Today: Same contradictory banner; still GOVERNS Spec 123 (123:12).
decisions.recommendation: **Recommendation.** Make Spec 121 **historical**, with the same banner clean-up as Spec 120. This needs the Spec 123 ruling below in the same change. Otherwise a historical spec would still "govern" an active one, and that contradicts R-GW ("a historical spec decides nothing"). Any Spec 121 content that is still true and still enforced already lives in Spec 123 §6 (the gates) or in Spec 132 lines (the M-items). Nothing needs to move first.

decisions.question: Role of Spec 123: Step Optimization: Assessment & Validation (431 lines). Today: ACTIVE; G0–G9 enforced by step-validate; listed as a historical record in rule-map meta.
decisions.recommendation:
**Recommendation.** Spec 123 can't be historical while its G0–G9 gates are enforced. Choose one:
- **(a) Recommended: make Spec 123 a standard**, the procedure half of the step family, and take it off `historical_design_records`. Its role banner would read roughly: "Role: standard. The conversion procedure and the G0–G9 gates step-validate computes; on policy the Spec 124 register governs (R-GV)." Line 12 changes from "Spec 121 is the method and GOVERNS this document" to "Spec 121 is the historical method record this procedure instantiates; on policy the Spec 124 register governs, on the schema and behaviour Spec 122." Spec 123 has a hand-written budget (423 lines / 49,705 B measured, +10%), so this costs about one line.
- **(b) Move §6 (the G0–G9 table) into Spec 124 or 122 through a spec-split register move, then make Spec 123 historical.** This costs more: 59 code citations to `Spec 123 §6` would need re-pointing or a stub.

Under (a), the steps family has three live specs: Spec 122 (standard: schema and behaviour), Spec 123 (standard: conversion procedure) and Spec 124 (register: policy). Spec 132 is generated from them. Under (b) the family stays a pair.
decisions.summary_recommendation: (a) standard (procedure), 123:12 rewritten, removed from `historical_design_records`; or (b) move §6, then historical
